trust_decision.summary: Playlist ownership is decided from the first path segment of the client-supplied, base64-decoded playlist id (userIDFromPath on the raw, uncleaned relPath in Store.Read), and the same raw id is joined onto the playlists base dir without containment; getPlaylist/deletePlaylist apply no owner check at all.

landing_point.why: Summary names playlist `id` and read/delete of other users' playlists; ServeGetPlaylist/ServeDeletePlaylist are the handlers that take `id` and lack an owner check.

fix_sites.entry_point: /rest/createPlaylist with id (err != nil inverted, so existing owner never loaded and owner check at :84 never fires)
Store.Read UserID/Name derived from cleaned rel path, reached by getPlaylist/updatePlaylist/createPlaylist/deletePlaylist
new SafeJoin helper built on HasPrefix (fix.diff:31-37)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: playlist/playlist.go:108 (userIDFromPath on raw relPath via firstPathEl playlist/playlist.go:209-220); fix at fix.diff:58-72

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The handlers already compare playlist.UserID with the caller (handlers_playlist.go:84, :138), so a solver adding handler checks sees ownership as 'enforced' and leaves the Store's identity parser alone; and getCoverArt for a playlist only returns a decoded image of a cover-named file, which looks like a cosmetic neighbouring feature, not playlist access.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Other users must still read PUBLIC playlists; legacy playlists with no numeric user dir fall back to user 1; nested sub-dirs under <user id>/**/ are a supported layout; m3u item lines may be relative (including ../) to the playlist dir. A fix that rejects any '/' or '..' in the id, or blocks all non-owner reads, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: id whose first segment is the caller's user id followed by ../<victim id>/name.m3u (identity spoof, stays inside base)
id with leading ../ that escapes the playlists base (read/write/delete outside base)
plain victim path <victim id>/name.m3u with no traversal (missing owner check on get/delete)
